result.topic_en: Euler derives a quartic equation in v and z from a condition for two triangles, generates successive rational solutions by chord/tangent-type recurrences for chosen alpha, beta, lists sequences of values for several cases, and extracts a numerical solution for p, q, r, s.
result.transcription:
Fragmenta ex Adversariis depromta. 223

$\frac{tt}{rr}=\frac{\alpha v^3-n\beta}{\alpha^3 v-n\beta^3}=\left(\frac{v}{\alpha}-z\right)^2,$
unde oritur haec aequatio
$0=n\beta-n\beta^3zz+\frac{2n\beta^3vz}{\alpha}+\alpha^3vzz-2\alpha\alpha vvz-\frac{n\beta^3vv}{\alpha\alpha},$
unde patet si $v=0$, fore $z=\pm\frac{1}{\beta}$; at si $z=0$, tum erit $v=\pm\frac{\alpha}{\beta}$, unde sequentes valores inveniuntur ope harum formularum $z+z'=\frac{2v}{\alpha},\ v+v'=\frac{\alpha z(2n\beta^3+\alpha^3z)}{n\beta^3+2\alpha^3z}.$
At vero si sumamus $v=\infty$, erit $z=\frac{-n\beta^3}{2\alpha^4},\ v=\frac{4\alpha^8-nn\beta^8}{3n\alpha^3\beta^5}.$
Quia hic litteras $\alpha$ et $\beta$ pro lubitu assumere licet, fortasse hinc novi valores eliciuntur, quos praecedens methodus non dat.

Si ex. gr. $\alpha=1$ et $\beta=2$, ut sit $q=t$ et $s=2t$, tum vero
$\frac{p}{r}=v$ et $\frac{t}{r}=v-z$, erit $z+z'=2v$ et $v+v'=\frac{z(z+16)}{2z+8}.$
Hinc sumto $v=0$, erit $z=\pm\frac{1}{2}$; at si $z=0$ erit $v=\pm\frac{1}{2}$. Praeterea si $v=\infty$, erit $z=-4$ et sequens $v=-\frac{21}{8}$, ex quibus casibus sequentes valores oriuntur
$v=\infty,\ z=-4,\ v=-\frac{21}{8},\ z=-\frac{5}{4},\ v=-\frac{8}{11},\ z=-\frac{9}{44},\ v=\frac{403}{8.167},$
tum vero $z=0,\ v=\frac{1}{2},\ z=1,\ v=\frac{6}{5},\ z=\frac{7}{5},\ v=\frac{19}{18},$
porro $z=0,\ v=-\frac{1}{2},\ z=-1,\ v=2,\ z=-3,\ v=-\frac{35}{2},\ z=-32,\ v=\frac{117}{14}$, etc.
$v=0,\ z=\frac{1}{2},\ v=\frac{11}{12},\ z=\frac{4}{3},\ v=\frac{5}{4},\ z=\frac{7}{6},\ v=\frac{64}{93}$, etc.
$v=0,\ z=-\frac{1}{2},\ v=-\frac{31}{23},\ z=-\frac{12}{7},\ v=-\frac{17}{4}.$
Casu $n=1$, valores $v$ et $z$ ita se habebunt:
$v=0,\ 1,\ 0,\ 1,\ \frac{8}{7},\ 1,\ \frac{104}{105},\ 1$
$z=1,\ 1,\ -1,\ 3,\ -\frac{5}{7},\ \frac{19}{7},\ -\frac{11}{15},$
tum vero $z=0,\ 2,\ -\frac{4}{5},\ \frac{14}{5},\ -\frac{8}{11},\ 0,\ -2,\ 4,\ -\frac{2}{3},\ \frac{8}{3}$
$v=1,\ \frac{3}{5},\ 1,\ \frac{57}{55},\ 1,\ -1,\ 1,\ \frac{5}{3},\ 1,\ \frac{55}{57}.$
Tum $v=\infty,\ 1,\ \frac{7}{8},\ 1,\ \frac{105}{104},\ 1,\ \frac{1455}{1456},\ 1,\ \frac{11.19.97}{16.7.181}=\frac{20271}{20272}$
$z=-\frac{1}{2},\ \frac{5}{2},\ -\frac{3}{4},\ \frac{11}{4},\ -\frac{19}{26},\ \frac{71}{28},\ -\frac{41}{56},\ \frac{153}{56}.$
Ita ex casu $v=\frac{1455}{1456}=\frac{3.5.97}{16.7.13}$ valores pro $p,\ q,\ r,\ s$ erunt: $p=3.5.97,\ q=2521,\ r=16.7.13,\ s=2521,$
$p+q=8.7.71,\ p-q=2.13.41,\ r+s=41.97,\ r-s=3.5.71$, ubi factores utrinque se mutuo destruunt.
A. m. T. III. p. 143.

methods.what: Reduction of the condition to a quartic in v and z
Recurrence (Vieta-root switching) generating new rational solutions from known ones
Numerical solution p,q,r,s with factorizations of sums and differences

items.quote: Quia hic litteras $\alpha$ et $\beta$ pro lubitu assumere licet, fortasse hinc novi valores eliciuntur, quos praecedens methodus non dat.
items.english: Since here the letters alpha and beta may be taken at will, perhaps new values are obtained from this which the preceding method does not give.
